title: Redwood All-Hands - March 2026
customer_attendees: Engineering, Product, Sales, Go-to-market, Research, Security
summary: Quarterly company all-hands covering Q1 performance, product milestones (Dedicated autoscaling, Private 1.2), cost optimization work, hiring update, and OKR refresh. Leadership answered questions about roadmap prioritization, enterprise security offerings, and compensation timing. Action items include updated docs for Private onboarding and a customer success outreach list for key accounts.
topics: Product: Dedicated autoscaling, Private 1.2 release, Optimize features
next_steps: Priya to publish Private 1.2 release notes and migration guide by 2026-03-18
Noah to send targeted customer outreach list for top 25 accounts by 2026-03-16
Ethan to schedule deep-dive on autoscaler behavior with infra team and SEs week of 2026-03-15
action_items: Priya Patel - Publish Private 1.2 release notes & migration guide - due 2026-03-18
Noah Kim - Create top-25 enterprise outreach list and messaging - due 2026-03-16
Ethan Ross - Run autoscaler post-mortem and share notes - due 2026-03-20
Maya Singh - Coordinate demo playbook for Dedicated upsell - due 2026-03-22

transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining. We'll kick off the March all-hands. Quick note, audio recorded. Uh, we'll run about an hour, try to leave time for Q&A.
[00:18] Marcus Alvarez: Hey all, quick infra update before numbers — two infra incidents in Feb, both around a spike in egress on hosted clusters, root cause was an NFS mount flapping during a rolling update, that led to degraded KV cache warmups and a small latency blip. We've patched the orchestration script and added guardrails, ETA for full rollout is end of week.
[01:05] Priya Patel: Product highlights — Private 1.2 is code complete, main features are VPC peering simplification, layered RBAC, and improved on-prem packaging for air-gapped installs. We'll be doing internal dogfood this week. There is a known issue where older quantized models need an adapter shim, we'll include migration steps in the release notes.
[01:42] Ethan Ross: On Dedicated autoscaling, we're seeing better tail latency at 95th p95 under the new batching policy, but some customers reported cold-starts on heavy short-request workloads. We're adding a warm pool option and a faster KV prefetch path to mitigate.
[02:20] Laura Chen: Business update — revenue continue to track up vs plan, up 18% QoQ in ARR motion, sign-ups for Dedicated are ahead of Q4 but conversion time is still longer than ideal. Our net retention for the quarter looks strong at ~112% but some renewals were pushed. Olivia will go through the finances.
[02:58] Olivia Park: Thanks. Quick highlights: burn rate down 7% sequentially, hiring momentum is slower but we have fewer contractor spend. Guidance for next quarter is conservative; focusing on expanding enterprise deals and Dedicated commitments to improve predictability. We'll post the detailed deck in #all-hands after.
[03:35] Maya Singh: Sales — pipeline healthy, notable wins include two mid-market PLG companies moving to Dedicated trials, and one financial services POC for Private in Europe. We still see procurement cycles stretching 8-12 weeks for regulated accounts. Pricing ask is common—customers want predictable per-instance pricing for Dedicated pools.
[04:05] Noah Kim: CS update — we're rolling out a proactive health-check cadence for top 25 customers, focusing on latency SLOs and cost regression alerts. Also starting a pilot for a shared benchmarking spreadsheet to help customers decide between hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[04:40] Priya Patel: Quick product roadmap callouts — next 90 days: 1) Private 1.2 GA and migration docs, 2) Dedicated autoscaler warm-pool opt-in, 3) Redwood Optimize: feature flags for predicted batching & cost limiters, 4) Observability: token-level cost drilldowns in Console.
[05:12] Attendee (Q): Is there an ETA on SOC 2 re-audit?
[05:15] Laura Chen: We started pre-audit in Feb, auditor engagement scheduled mid-April, expect certification early May. We will publish scope and changes to the security page.
[05:36] Attendee (Q): Any update on region expansion to APAC?
[05:40] Marcus Alvarez: Yes, partner region in APAC is live in preview, latency targets are okay for most customers but we need test coverage for Private on-prem in APAC. We'll announce the general availability once we complete two more partner validations.
[06:05] Speaker 3: There's a question about cost-of-inference tooling — like, how soon can customers see batching suggestions?
[06:12] Priya Patel: We're shipping Optimize beta for self-serve accounts in April; it will surface batching and quantization suggestions and expected unit-cost delta. Early beta partners already see 12-25% improvements on steady-state workloads.
[06:40] Laura Chen: Hiring — engineering freeze lifted for SRE and runtime teams, we're prioritizing senior infra and runtime engineers, recruiter pipeline is open. Compensation cycles — we plan to discuss equity refresh timing with managers next week.
[07:05] Ethan Ross: Reliability incident review — the larger Feb incident had 11 minutes of elevated error rates for a small subset of routes. Root cause: worker restarts during shard rebalancing. We've queued a k8s pre-drain hook and will add canary logic to the rollout pipeline.
[07:38] Speaker 4: Any changes to the roadmap after the infra issues?
[07:42] Priya Patel: Slight reprioritization — we moved planned non-essential UX polish to next quarter to accelerate autoscaler and Private migrations.
[08:00] Laura Chen: For GTM: Maya, Noah, please coordinate on the outreach and the demo playbook for Dedicated upsell. Also, we want a short case study for the two wins that moved from hosted to Dedicated — marketing to run with that.
[08:20] Maya Singh: Will do. We'll pull demo metrics and pricing comparisons, should have a draft by end of next week.
[08:30] Attendee (Q): Any legal/process blockers for Private on-prem customers?
[08:34] Olivia Park: Standard NDAs and SOC2 review are the frequent items; for some regulated customers we need HSM/KMS integrations and we have a template in progress. Procurement tends to be the slowest part.
[08:50] Crowd murmur / crosstalk: (laughter)
[09:05] Marcus Alvarez: Tech highlight — model onboarding pipeline now supports quantization-aware conversion and a small validation harness that runs perf/latency tests across sample sequences. That has reduced manual tuning time by about 40% for the model team.
[09:42] Priya Patel: On the roadmap item about Console improvements — token-level cost explorer is higher priority, will kick off design this sprint. We'll need PM/UX/Platform pairing to define the API surface.
[10:05] Attendee raised hand: What about the Dedicated pricing changes we discussed?
[10:10] Olivia Park: We're considering a two-tier pricing for Dedicated: reserved committed tier and burst on-demand; the goal is to give customers predictable committed price while allowing burst for short workloads. We'll share scenarios and modeling next week.
[10:38] Laura Chen: OK let's open to Q&A — please drop questions in the chat or raise hands.
[10:50] [11:12] Q&A segment: multiple short questions about demo scripts, marketing assets, and Manager level OKR alignment. Some cross-talk, a few people on phone so speaker labels show as Speaker 6 / Speaker 7.
[20:05] Speaker 6: Quick ask — can design team allocate a sprint for Console usability fixes?
[20:12] Priya Patel: Yes we can allocate 20% capacity next sprint to address top-10 issues, will publish a list.
[25:00] Speaker 7: Is there a plan to support more open model variants in the catalog?
[25:05] Marcus Alvarez: Yes, model catalog expansion is ongoing; regulatory selection and benchmarking are the gating items. We have a partner evaluation for two new quantized variants next month.
[30:10] Laura Chen: Wrap up — appreciate the progress and the hard work; we will share the slide deck, the recording, and action items in #all-hands. Reminder: company offsite planning starts next quarter, please complete the interest survey.
[30:35] End of meeting recording.
